label: Fetch a consumable

equipment.description: The catalogue model to take from the store: a tube, plate, flask, cuvette …

id.description: The id the new container gets

fill.description: { preparation, amount }: fetched ready-filled from the stockroom

description: Take an empty container from the store and put it on the bench. Logistics: whether it costs the learner time depends on the support profile.

label: Transfer a liquid

tool.description: A pipette, burette, volumetric pipette or inoculating loop instance; omitted = poured

technique.description: Technique-quality inputs from the interaction: prewet, immersion, speed, angle

mode.description: Air-displacement pipettes: reverse pipetting (aspirate past the first stop, dispense only to it) keeps viscous or foaming liquids accurate

all.description: Pour out everything that drains (no tool, no volume): the vessel keeps its dead volume and a film on its walls

spot.description: Onto an agar plate: the numbered spot (1-48) the drop stays in, its colonies counted apart (a spot plate)

brim.description: Pour until the destination runs over, leaving no air in it (a BOD bottle or density bottle); give no volume or tool

description: Aspirate from the source and dispense into the destination. Refuses only the physically impossible (volume outside the tool's range, no tip, too little liquid, overflow, a closed container). Delivered volume carries the tool's systematic and random error; a reused tip carries a film of its last liquid. Onto an agar plate, cells stay on the surface; into a gel well, a sample without about 3 % glycerol floats away.

label: Add a solid

mass.description: About how much to take; required unless all is true

all.description: Scrape out everything (from a container); a wet solid carries its liquid, and a filter paper keeps a little

description: Add a solid from a stock bottle or another container with a spatula. The amount actually added differs slightly from the intended mass; weighing tells the learner what they really have. A scoop of a wet solid carries its liquid with it.

label: Lift pieces out with forceps

source.description: The vessel the pieces lie in

destination.description: Where they go: a weighing boat, a tile, another liquid

substance.description: Only pieces of this (by default, every solid piece)

blot.description: Blot them on paper towel first, leaving only a thin film of the liquid

description: Take solid pieces (tissue cylinders or discs, a metal strip, marble chips) out of a liquid with forceps into another vessel. They bring a film of the liquid, much less once blotted, and their heat.

label: Read a volume
description: Read the scale of a graduated vessel at eye level. Burettes read from the top; the reading carries a small parallax error and is rounded to the half-graduation.

label: Read a balance
description: Read the load on the balance pan (minus its tare) as a measurement record, at the balance's readability.

label: Mix
description: Homogenise a container's contents and dissolve soluble solids. Each method mixes a fraction per cycle.

label: Make up to the mark
description: Fill a volumetric container to its calibration mark. The final volume is the nominal volume within the class tolerance (meniscus reading error).

label: Place in

position.description: Position in an instrument with slots (rotor positions 1..n); default the first free one

description: Put a container (or plate) into a place: an incubator, water bath, ice, a balance pan, an instrument. Its temperature then moves towards the place's.

label: Take out
description: Return a container to the bench.

label: Set a device

distance.description: A lamp: its distance from what it lights (light falls as the square of the distance)

filter.description: A lamp: a coloured filter in front of it

humidity.description: The air: relative humidity, 0 to 1 (a plastic bag over a plant raises it to about 0.95)

wind.description: The air: a fan blowing across, low or high

description: Change a device's setpoint (incubator, water bath, heating block).

label: Let time pass
description: Integrate every time-dependent process (temperature, mixing by diffusion, degradation, reactions, colour development) over simulated time.

label: Centrifuge

rcf.description: Relative centrifugal force, e.g. "12000 [RCF]"; or give rpm

rpm.description: Rotor speed in revolutions per minute, converted through the centrifuge's rotor radius (RCF = 1.118e-5 × r(cm) × rpm²)

description: Spin the loaded rotor. An unbalanced rotor stops with an incident and nothing separates; open tubes spill. Sedimentation is T1 (settled solids, clear supernatant). Cells pellet by the centrifugal dose and the square of their size (5 µm algae or yeast at about 1000 × g in minutes; bacteria need several thousand × g for ten minutes); mixing resuspends them.

label: Measure

instrument.description: A spectrophotometer, plate reader, pH meter, microscope, melting-point apparatus, colony counter, UV lamp, gel imager, sequencer, IR spectrometer, dissolved-oxygen meter, mass spectrometer, fluorimeter, voltmeter, conductivity meter, pressure sensor, ruler or hand lens (flies)

wavelength.description: The wavelength read (spectrophotometers) or the excitation wavelength (fluorimeters)

mode.description: Spectrophotometers: one reading, a time course (kinetic), or a spectrum across from-to (scan)

squares.description: Counting chambers: how many large squares to count (default 4)

conditions.description: Mass spectrometers: sprayed from acidic organic solvent (proteins unfold, many charges) or a volatile native buffer (fewer charges)

from.description: Scans and fluorimeter emission: the shortest wavelength

to.description: Scans and fluorimeter emission: the longest wavelength

electrode.description: Voltmeters: the metal the positive (red) lead is on, where the vessel holds more than one

negative.description: Voltmeters: the vessel the negative (black) lead’s electrode is in (the same vessel if left out)

negativeElectrode.description: Voltmeters: the metal the negative lead is on, where its vessel holds more than one

description: Run an instrument on a container, plate or slide. Produces raw measurement records (or, for a microscope, an observation of shapes and colours); nothing is corrected automatically.

label: Calibrate an instrument

buffers.description: Two-point pH calibration: two buffers with labelled pH

description: Set an instrument reference: blank a spectrophotometer against a reference cuvette, or calibrate a pH meter with two buffers (the meter then maps the electrode onto the buffers labelled pH, right or wrong).

position.description: Where on the item: its label area, or (slides) the middle, where the light passes

label: Dispose

container.description: What to empty and throw away (or give an item instead)

item.description: A used tool to throw away: a syringe and needle into the sharps bin

description: Empty a container's contents into a waste stream. Disposal events are kept so that disposal can be assessed.

label: Set a pipette's volume
description: Dial a variable pipette. Refused outside the pipette's range (it cannot be dialled there).

cover.description: The vessel's own cap or stopper, a square of Parafilm (for cuvettes, beakers and tubes without one), or a rubber septum that a needle can pass through

label: Purge with inert gas

container.description: A flask sealed with a septum

balloon.description: A balloon of nitrogen (or argon) on a needle

duration.description: How long the gas flows out through the vent needle

sparge.description: Bubble the gas through the liquid too, taking out its dissolved oxygen

description: Flushes the air out of a septum-sealed flask with an inert gas from a balloon, a vent needle letting it out; the balloon stays on, so the flask stays under the gas as liquid is drawn from it. With sparging, the gas is bubbled through the liquid and takes the dissolved oxygen with it.

label: Flush a syringe with inert gas

source.description: A septum-sealed flask under an inert gas, its balloon on

description: Draws gas from the headspace of a flask kept under nitrogen and pushes it out, three times, so the syringe carries no air into what it is used for. From a flask without a balloon, air comes in behind the gas.

label: Record a value

source.description: The measurement record this value was read from

description: Write a value into the notebook, linked to its source measurement if any.

label: Lay out a plate

groups.description: Items to place: { group, items: [containers], role? }

description: Assign wells to standards, samples, replicates and blanks. The plan is data the later steps follow.

input.description: A measurement record, or values by well

layout.description: The plate layout (which wells are blanks and replicates)

window.description: Initial-rate window from the start of a kinetic read

recordAs.description: Optionally record inputs and outputs atomically in this notebook field

label: Fit a model

z.description: A second independent variable for each point: the inhibitor concentration, for model inhibition

recordAs.description: Optionally record inputs and outputs atomically in this notebook field

sources.description: Displayed measurement references used by the learner

description: A four-parameter logistic (four-pl: y = d + (a − d)/(1 + (x/c)^b)) suits binding assays such as an ELISA, whose response levels off at both ends; samples are read only between 10 and 90 % of its rise. The inhibition model fits rates at several substrate (x) and inhibitor (z) concentrations to the competitive, uncompetitive, non-competitive and mixed mechanisms at once, and keeps the one with the lowest AICc (its fit names the mechanism: inhibition-competitive and so on).

label: Run a statistical test

groups.description: The groups' values (t-tests, ANOVA), or the rows of counts of a contingency table

x.description: One-sample t: the values; regression: the independent variable

mu.description: One-sample t: the mean tested against

expected.description: Chi-square: the expected counts or proportions

description: Outputs the statistic (t, F or chi-square), its degrees of freedom (df, and df2 for ANOVA), the p-value (two-sided for t and the slope), each group's mean, the difference or slope with its 95 % confidence interval, and whether p is below alpha.

points.description: Readings, or group means from average-replicates

recordAs.description: Optionally record inputs and outputs atomically in this notebook field

sources.description: Displayed measurement references used by the learner

report.description: { quantity, sample }: the value is this run's reported result for that sample

recordAs.description: Optionally record inputs and outputs atomically in this notebook field

label: Propagate uncertainty

expression.description: The result, as an expression of the named inputs

uncertainties.description: Each input's standard uncertainty, in its own units (a ±a tolerance is a/√3)

coverage.description: Coverage factor k for the expanded uncertainty U = k·u

description: An uncertainty budget by the law of propagation of uncertainty (first order, independent inputs): the combined standard uncertainty, the expanded uncertainty, and each input's share of the variance, so the dominant source stands out.

label: Dry
description: Dry a container's liquid at the method's rate (air: about 20 µL/min; heat: about 200 µL/min); without a duration, to dryness. Dissolved solutes stay behind as solid, and what exceeds its solubility comes out as the liquid shrinks; cells become a film on the surface. Air-dried cells are only loosely attached and wash off; heat fixes them (and kills them).

label: Flood with a reagent
description: Cover a slide with a reagent (about 0.5 mL) for a time. Stains act on the cells according to the staining model; liquid over unfixed cells lifts some of them off.

label: Rinse with water
description: Rinse a slide or surface with a gentle stream of water: loose liquid goes, and so do most unfixed cells.

label: Flame a loop or spreader

tool.description: An inoculating loop, needle, spreader or forceps

description: Heat a loop to red heat: whatever it carried is destroyed. An unflamed loop carries organisms from one culture to the next.

label: Apply a disc (antibiotic, mutagen or control)

disc.description: A paper disc carrying an antibiotic or a mutagen (or only water, as a control)

position.description: Position 1–6 round the plate (default: the next free one)

description: Presses a disc onto the agar: what it carries starts diffusing outwards at once, while the cells grow. Apply antibiotic discs within about 15 minutes of seeding; a disc put on late leaves a smaller zone. A mutagen acts on the cells as they divide, and kills where it is concentrated.

label: Spot test (catalase, oxidase …)

reagent.description: The test reagent (a drop is used)

target.description: A culture, a slide, or a plate

appearance.description: On a plate: test the colonies that look like this

description: A drop of reagent on cells shows whether they have the trait the test detects (bubbles for catalase, a purple colour for oxidase). A mixture gives a weak, patchy reaction; too few cells give nothing readable.

label: Filter

source.description: Pour everything from this vessel onto the filter first; omitted = drain what is already on it (after a wash)

filter.description: A filter funnel with paper (Büchner or gravity)

description: Solids stay on the filter; the liquid passes into the filtrate except what the wet cake holds (about 1 mL per gram on a Büchner funnel under vacuum, 2 mL per gram by gravity), with whatever is dissolved in it. Liquid on the filter mixes with the cake and reaches solubility equilibrium before it drains.

label: Drain through the tap

funnel.description: A separating funnel (a vessel with a tap), unstoppered

volume.description: Run off this much from the bottom; omitted = the lower layer, the tap closed at the interface

description: Runs liquid out of the bottom of a separating funnel. By default the lower layer goes, the tap closed as the interface reaches it, so a little of that layer stays behind; with a volume, that much leaves from the bottom, through the interface if need be. The stopper must be out for air to get in.

label: Concentrate (rotary evaporator)

flask.description: The round-bottom flask holding the solution

duration.description: How long it turns in the bath under vacuum

description: Turns the flask in a warm bath under reduced pressure. Volatile solvents distil off, a solvent layer taking the water dissolved in it; water standing as its own layer goes only slowly. What does not evaporate is left on the glass: the crude product, with anything that came through the work-up with it.

label: Distil

volume.description: Distillate to collect in this fraction

column.description: A fractionating column between the flask and the still head (none: simple distillation)

description: Boils the pot and collects the condensed vapour: richer in the more volatile component than the pot, and richer still through a fractionating column, up to any azeotrope. The pot is depleted as it goes, so later fractions are poorer and the still head hotter; never distil to dryness.

label: Blot a gel onto a membrane
description: Every lane's protein bands move onto the membrane at the same positions (about an hour in the tank); large proteins transfer less completely.

label: Develop and photograph a blot

membrane.description: A blot lying in a chromogenic substrate

description: Colour builds up where enzyme-labelled antibody is bound: bands where the antibodies found their target, and a background wherever antibody stuck to unblocked membrane. A prestained marker shows on its own.

label: Spot a TLC plate

lane.description: Lane on the origin line, from the left

description: A small volume of solution onto one lane's origin; the solvent evaporates and the solutes stay on the silica. Loading more makes a bigger spot that runs into its neighbours.

label: Develop a TLC plate

chamber.description: A chamber with the eluent in it

front.description: How far the solvent front runs from the origin before the plate is taken out

description: Each compound travels a fraction of the solvent front's distance, its Rf, which falls the more strongly silica holds it and rises with the eluent's strength. If the eluent stands above the origin, the spots dissolve into it instead.

label: Wash wells

target.description: A plate (every well in use) or one well or tube

description: Empty each well, fill it with buffer and empty it again, as many times as asked. What is stuck to the wall (adsorbed protein, bound antibody) stays; what is free is diluted away by the few microlitres a well keeps each time.

label: Collect a fraction from a column

column.description: A size-exclusion or affinity column; liquid on its bed runs in first

buffer.description: The running buffer pushed through the column

into.description: The tube that collects this fraction

description: Each solute leaves the column around its elution volume, which falls with its native size across the matrix's fractionation range: large molecules with the void volume, small ones (salts) with the total bed volume. Bands spread with the column's plate count and with the sample's own volume. On an affinity column, the liquid on the bed (and any buffer asked for; the volume may be 0) passes through: tagged proteins stay until enough competitor (imidazole) frees them, and the rest flows out into the fraction.

label: Run an analytical column (UV monitor)

column.description: An analytical size-exclusion column, equilibrated in running buffer

wavelengths.description: Wavelengths to record (nm), from those the monitor offers; default 280

runVolume.description: How much buffer to run through; default the column volume and 2 mL more

description: Injects a sample on an analytical size-exclusion column and records the absorbance of the eluate against the volume passed: each solute a peak at its elution volume, large ones first, sized by how strongly it absorbs at each wavelength. The sample goes to waste.

label: Spread a plate
description: Spread the cells on an agar plate so that colonies grow apart; unspread cells grow where the drop sat and their colonies run together. The spreader leaves on this plate what it carried from the last one, and takes away a little of this one, until it is sterilised.

label: Streak a sector

sector.description: 1 for the inoculum, then 2, 3, 4 … each drawn out of the one before

cross.description: Whether the stroke crosses the previous sector (a dilution streak); false streaks a separate patch, as when several cultures share a plate

description: Streak one sector of a plate. Sector 1 spreads the inoculum; each later sector drags about 2 % of the previous sector's cells, plus whatever the loop still carries, so flaming the loop between sectors is what leaves single colonies at the end.

label: Pick a colony

destination.description: Broth, or a drop of water on a slide; left out, the cells stay on the loop (to streak or stab with)

appearance.description: Which kind of colony to pick, by its look ("golden")

description: Touch a colony with the loop and put the cells (about 10⁷) into a liquid, or keep a loopful on the loop. From a sector of separate colonies the pick is one strain; from crowded growth (or a slope) it is a mixture.

label: Run a PCR program

threshold.description: Real-time cyclers: the baseline-corrected signal (ΔRn) at which a well's Cq is read

description: Run a program on every tube in the cycler, then hold. Each cycle copies every target whose two primers are present; the efficiency falls if annealing is above the primers' Tm, if extension is too short for the product, or if denaturation is too cool; primers and nucleotides limit the yield; low annealing temperatures make primer-dimers. A real-time cycler also reads every well after each cycle and records its baseline-corrected signal and Cq (Undetermined if it never crosses the threshold).

label: Run a melt curve

cycler.description: A real-time cycler holding the finished reactions

description: Heats every reaction slowly while reading the dye. Each duplex melts at its own temperature, so the negative derivative of the signal (−dF/dT) has a peak per product: one sharp peak for a single amplicon, a lower and broader one for primer-dimers.

label: Run a gel

voltage.description: Volts; negative if the leads are swapped (the DNA runs out of the wells)

description: DNA in each loaded lane runs towards the anode at a speed that falls with the log of its length (range set by the agarose percentage). Bands that run past the end are lost.

label: Set an instrument's controls

objective.description: Microscopes: the objective to turn into the light path (4x, 10x, 40x, 100x-oil …), or none to turn the nosepiece between objectives

illumination.description: Microscopes: the condenser turret, brightfield or a phase annulus (ph1, ph2 …) matching the objective's phase ring

lamp.description: Lamp output as a fraction of full (0 to 1); higher power needs more light

condenser.description: Microscopes: condenser focused on the field, or left as found (uneven light, poorer resolution)

description: Set controls that persist on the instrument. Microscopes: objective, illumination, lamp and condenser. Turning a high-power dry objective over a slide with immersion oil on it takes the lens into the oil.

label: Focus a microscope
description: Coarse focus finds the specimen at low power; at high power (working distance under 1 mm) it drives the slide into the lens and cracks it. Fine focus sharpens an image that is nearly in focus and cannot find one that is not. Objectives are parfocal: after turning the nosepiece the image is nearly in focus.

label: Clean oil off a lens

objective.description: One objective; left out, every objective with oil on it

slide.description: Also wipe the immersion oil off this slide

description: Wipe immersion oil off with lens tissue. Oil left on a dry objective blurs every image through it.

label: Flame the neck of a bottle or tube
description: Pass the open neck through a hot flame, after opening and before closing. An uncovered vessel's rim, handled unflamed, now and then lets a contaminant in (contract contamination).

label: Clean your hands
description: Wash at the sink, or use an antiseptic wipe: fewer skin organisms are left on the fingers.

label: Press fingertips on agar

plate.description: An agar plate with its lid off

description: One gentle press of the fingertips on the agar: the skin flora the hands carry now is left on it.

label: Stab an agar deep

source.description: A broth culture to dip the loop into first; left out, the loop's own load is stabbed

description: Plunge the loaded loop straight down the middle of the agar. Where it grows along the stab shows the organism's oxygen requirement.

label: Search references with a sequence

query.description: A sequence: plain bases or FASTA

description: Compare a sequence with the reference sequences, on both strands (an offline stand-in for a nucleotide BLAST). Outputs the hits ranked by score, each with its title, identity (%), query coverage (%), strand, the span it aligns to and the annotated genes there; `top` and `gene` are the best hit and its first gene.

label: Align two sequences

query.description: A sequence: plain bases or FASTA

subject.description: A second sequence, or the id of a reference sequence

gene.description: The gene whose coding sequence numbers the codons (default: the one the alignment falls in)

description: Align two sequences locally (pairwise, BLASTN scores, both strands). Outputs identity and coverage, and each difference: substitution, insertion or deletion, its position in each sequence, and (against an annotated reference) the codon and its effect: silent, missense (Leu69Pro), nonsense, a frameshift with the residues it changes before a stop, or an in-frame loss or gain.

label: Connect the gas

container.description: The vessel the gas comes from

syringe.description: A gas syringe on a bung: it collects the gas to be read

into.description: Another vessel's liquid for the gas to bubble through (limewater)

description: Fit a bung: to a gas syringe, which collects the gas given off so its volume can be read (from zero now), or to a delivery tube into another liquid, which the gas bubbles through. With neither, the bung comes off and the gas goes to the room.

label: Fit a still head and condenser

flask.description: The flask to distil from (it is heated where it stands)

receiver.description: Where the condensed vapour runs (omit to take the still head off again)

description: Set a flask up for distillation into a receiver: while it boils (at the bubble point of what it holds), the vapour, richer in what boils lower, is condensed into the receiver, so a product that boils below the mixture leaves as it forms. Without a receiver the still head comes off, and the head temperatures and the volume that came over are reported.

label: Test the gas

container.description: The vessel whose gas is tested at its mouth

description: Hold a lighted splint, a glowing splint or damp litmus paper at the mouth of the vessel and see what happens: hydrogen pops, oxygen relights a glowing splint, carbon dioxide puts a flame out, ammonia turns red litmus blue.

label: Flame test

sample.description: The solution or solid the wire is dipped in

wire.description: A nichrome or platinum wire loop

view.description: By eye, through cobalt-blue glass (which hides sodium's yellow), or through a hand spectroscope (the bright lines and their wavelengths)

clean.description: Clean the wire first: dip it in concentrated hydrochloric acid and heat it until it gives no colour

description: Dip the wire in the sample and hold it at the edge of a roaring Bunsen flame: each metal's atoms emit their own light (sodium yellow-orange, potassium lilac, lithium crimson, calcium orange-red, copper green). The colour comes from the emission lines, so a trace of sodium masks potassium, and cobalt-blue glass shows potassium through it. An uncleaned wire shows what it last held.

label: Connect a salt bridge

to.description: The other half-cell; leave out to take the bridge away

description: Lay a strip of filter paper soaked in potassium nitrate solution across two beakers so that it dips into both: ions can then move between the half-cells, completing the circuit without mixing them.

label: Electrolyse

cell.description: The vessel of electrolyte the electrodes dip into

anode.description: The electrode on the positive terminal (an electrode holder with its strip or rod)

cathode.description: The electrode on the negative terminal

current.description: The current set on the supply, e.g. 0.5 A

anodeGas.description: A tube full of the liquid upturned over the anode, to collect its gas (bung it to a gas syringe to measure the volume)

cathodeGas.description: A tube upturned over the cathode, to collect its gas

description: Pass a direct current through the electrolyte between two electrodes for a time. Metal ions or hydrogen are reduced at the cathode; the anode dissolves, or a halogen or oxygen forms there, whichever comes first. Reports the charge passed and what is seen at each electrode.

label: Trap air in a syringe

container.description: A gas syringe that can be sealed

volume.description: The volume of room air to draw in before capping the nozzle

description: Draw a volume of the room’s air into a gas syringe and cap its nozzle, trapping the gas (and any liquid already in it).

label: Hold the plunger

volume.description: Push or pull the plunger to this volume and hold it there; leave out to let it go free (atmospheric pressure)

description: Squeeze or expand the trapped gas to a volume and hold it there, or release the plunger so the gas finds its own volume at atmospheric pressure.

label: Add flies to a vial
description: Tip flies of a stock into a vial: virgin females and males, which mate and leave offspring a generation later if the vial is kept warm.

label: Move flies to another vial

females.description: How many females to move (as virgins)

phenotype.description: Only flies that look like this (e.g. "wild type", "vestigial wings")

description: Etherise flies and move some to a fresh vial as its parents: the offspring if they have emerged (the next generation), otherwise the adults; picked at random, or only those of one phenotype.

label: Set up a side of a choice chamber

humidity.description: Silica gel (dry) or damp paper (humid) under the gauze

description: Set the conditions on one side of a choice chamber: the humidity under its gauze and whether it is covered.

label: Put animals in a choice chamber
description: Put animals in through the centre hole of a choice chamber; they land on either side at random and then wander.
